description:
The surah that opens with a dire divine warning of a debasing punishment awaiting in the Hereafter for those who practice cheating as a norm in commerce, and whom is calls **The Defrauders** because they insist on receiving a full amount in return for the partial measure that they themselves give. It takes its name from verse 1, which condemns the tradesmen who cheat customers by using short weights and measures (muṭaffifūn). It appears that the practice of cheating have been prevalent in Mecca, and is strongly condemned here and elsewhere in the Quran (e.g. 11: 84 ff.; 7: 85).
The surah is also known as The Cheats, The Dealing in Fraud, The Defrauders, The Stinters, The Unjust, Those who Give Short Measure

translations.1: Woe to the defrauders who use short measures,
translations.3: but diminish when they measure or weigh for them.
translations.4: Do they not know that they will be resurrected
translations.6:
a day when mankind will stand
  before the Lord of all the worlds?
translations.7: No indeed! The record of the vicious is indeed in _Sijjīn_.
translations.8: And what will show you what is _Sijjīn_?
translations.10: Woe to the deniers on that day,
translations.11: who deny the Day of Retribution;
translations.12: and none denies it except every sinful transgressor.
translations.13:
When Our signs are recited to him,
  he says, 'Myths of the ancients!'
translations.14:
No indeed! Rather their hearts have been sullied<{["F", 1]}>
 by what they have been earning.
translations.15:
No indeed!
 They will be alienated from their Lord on that day.
translations.16: Then they will indeed enter hell,
translations.17:
then told,
   'This is what you used to deny!'
translations.18:
No indeed!
 The record of the pious is indeed in _Illīyūn_.
translations.19: And what will show you what is _Illīyūn_?
translations.21: witnessed by those brought near [to Allah].
translations.22: Indeed the pious shall be amid bliss,
translations.24: You will perceive in their faces the freshness of bliss
translations.25: as they are served with a sealed wine,
translations.26:
whose seal is musk
  —for such let the viers vie—
translations.28: a spring where those brought near [to Allah] drink.
translations.29:
Indeed the guilty
   used to laugh at the faithful,
translations.30:
and when they passed them
   by they would wink at each other,
translations.31:
and when they returned to their folks
   they would return rejoicing,
translations.32:
and when they saw them
   they would say,
  'Indeed those are the astray!'
translations.33: Though they were not sent to watch over them.
translations.34:
So today the faithful
   will laugh at the faithless,
translations.36:
Have the faithless been requited
  for what they used to do?
